source.title: Interpreting the Linear Structure of Vision-language Model Embedding Spaces
source.authors: Isabel Papadimitriou; Huang-Yuan Su; Thomas Fel; Naomi Saphra; S. Kakade; Stephanie Gil

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether learned SAE concepts are stable and finds that stability depends strongly on concept energy and training-data mixture, refining the claim that dictionary features are stable canonical units. It also applies SAE feature recovery to vision-language models.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test toy-model superposition, feature competition for limited capacity, or one-dimensional versus multidimensional feature geometry. The plotted reconstruction and modality results are included where they bear on SAE recovery or feature stability. The modality-cone and bridge-score analyses do not directly test another listed version.
record.test_reason: Section 4 retrains SAEs across 5 seeds and 7 image:text mixtures and measures dictionary stability. This bears directly on V5's claim that SAE features are stable units, and the study finds stability depends on concept energy. No other version is tested: the SAE-vs-Semi-NMF comparison is a method-selection result, the modality analyses measure a different construct, and the setting is VLM embedding spaces, not LLMs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE dictionaries vary across seeds and data mixtures, but the high-energy subset is consistently recovered and accounts for nearly all reconstruction. They conclude SAEs are reliable only when conditioned on energy. Concepts are mostly single-modality in usage but often lie near the modality-agnostic subspace; the authors attribute the modality score to SAE thresholding rather than direction. The Bridge Score reveals cross-modal concept links.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains BatchTopK SAEs and other dictionary-learning methods on VLM embedding spaces; it does not reproduce the toy-network method in Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Dictionary stability varies with concept energy; the learned concept modality distribution varies with the image:text training-data mixture.

fits_no_version.finding: BatchTopK SAEs with k=5 of 4,096 concepts reconstruct VLM embeddings better than Semi-NMF at fixed sparsity, across CLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2 and AIMv2. Values are figure-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse overcomplete dictionaries recover structure in multimodal (VLM) embedding spaces: an extension of V4 beyond LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE concepts are mostly single-modality in activation, yet many lie near the modality-agnostic subspace. The authors attribute apparent unimodality to TopK thresholding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-based selectivity of SAE features can be an artifact of the SAE's sparsity nonlinearity rather than of feature direction.

record.problems: The stability and mixture findings concern SAE dictionaries rather than the model's complete or canonical features. Several plotted comparisons provide no numerical values in the text. Results are for VLM embedding spaces, not LLM neuron activations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional version-relevant results left out. The paper's activation-cone, concept-classifier, bridge-score, and qualitative example analyses do not directly test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, sparsity transition or geometry analysis.
All of it: no test of capacity competition.
All of it: no analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
Not tested. Work is on VLM embedding spaces, not LLM neurons. The only reconstruction result is a method comparison, and spread across neurons is not measured.
Completeness and canonicality relative to the model's true features are not tested. Seed stability is measured on SigLIP2 only. Mixture stability is shown only qualitatively.
All of it: no comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: The study gives no numeric stability score across data mixtures; only UMAP visuals are shown. Rows should note that no quantitative mixture-stability value exists.

record.verdict_notes: Seed stability is SigLIP2 only, with 5 seeds. The 0.92 figure depends on a post-hoc energy cutoff (top 512). The study has no controls and reports no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric structure.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The models are VLMs and the study analyzes embedding spaces, not LLM internal neuron activations. It does not establish feature spread across neurons.
The study tests stability across seeds and data mixtures, but not whether SAE features are complete or canonical relative to the model's true features.
The study represents concepts as dictionary directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE concept modality scores and their energy-weighted distribution.
rows.value: Distribution is bimodal, with dominant modes near 0 and 1; energy is concentrated on concepts nearly exclusive to one modality
rows.note: Text describes this pattern across all four models; the figure gives the CLIP panel.
rows.check: The modality-score distribution measures modality selectivity of concepts. It is not evidence of features spread across neurons or of sparse-feature recovery, so it bears on no version.

rows.subject: SigLIP2
rows.operation_detail: Compared dictionaries from five independently trained SAEs using all concepts.
rows.note: The authors describe overall stability as low.
rows.check: Correctly linked. The stated value is mean pairwise stability 0.16 over all 4,096 concepts, SigLIP2 only, which the authors call low.

source_check.correct: State: partial. Mean pairwise stability is 0.16 across five SigLIP2 SAE dictionaries containing 4,096 concepts each; the authors describe this as low.
source_check.problem: Low stability establishes incomplete agreement; absence beyond a control is not established.

rows.subject: SigLIP2
rows.operation_detail: Compared dictionaries from five independently trained SAEs, restricted to the most energetic concepts.

conditions.value: top 512 energetic concepts from each run

rows.note: The paper characterizes high-energy concepts as remarkably stable.
rows.check: Value 0.92 holds only after restricting to each run's top-512 energetic concepts. This is a post-hoc subset, and the measurement is SigLIP2 only.

rows.subject: SigLIP2
rows.operation_detail: Measured concentration of activation energy across SAE concepts.
rows.value: Top 512 concepts account for approximately 99%; the other 3,500 account for 1%
rows.note: This reports how usage is concentrated and contextualizes the stability comparison.
rows.check: Energy concentration (top 512 concepts carry ~99% of activation mass) is context for r10, not itself a stability measure.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE dictionaries trained on different image:text mixtures.

conditions.value: Seven compositions ranging from 5:1 image:text to 1:5 image:text

rows.measure: Change in concept modality distribution across training mixtures
rows.value: The distribution shifts with the training mixture: text-heavy data yields more text concepts and image-heavy data yields more image concepts
rows.note: The paper says this sensitivity is especially associated with low-energy, rarely used concepts.
rows.check: The dictionary's modality composition shifts with the training mixture, so the full dictionary is not stable across data. This should be absent rather than partial. Evidence is qualitative UMAP with no number. The subject is the main Figure 3 model (unnamed); Figure 10 adds SigLIP2, SigLIP and CLIP.
